chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to us, from his father, from Wahb ibn Wahb al-Qadi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said:
God, exalted is His majesty, said: O son of Adam, obey Me in what I have commanded you, and do not teach Me what is good for you.

key_terms.أطعني: Obey Me - a divine command in the imperative form
key_terms.جل جلاله: Exalted is His majesty - a glorification formula for God
key_terms.يصلحك: What is good for you / what rectifies your affairs

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith qudsi say about obeying God's commands?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi (sacred divine saying) is transmitted through a chain from Imam al-Sadiq through his forefathers to the Prophet Muhammad. God commands the children of Adam to obey His directives without presuming to know better than their Creator what benefits them. Recorded in the fifty-second assembly of al-Shaykh al-Saduq's Amali (368 AH), it reinforces the foundational principle of complete submission to divine will.
